title: Running a tournament that keeps its own score
target: How to set up and run a TCG Card Shop Simulator tournament so the standings come out of the game's own scoring instead of your own notes on paper.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A prize shelf with prizes already on it
Enough customers in the shop to take part

steps.do: Put the prizes on the prize shelf before the first round rather than after the last one.
steps.because: a shelf dedicated to tournament prizes exists as its own shelf type (TournamentPrizeShelf)

steps.do: Make sure entrants can register before the opening round begins.
steps.because: an entrant's record tracks whether they registered for the start (CustomerTournamentData)

steps.do: Let the game score the rounds instead of keeping a tally of your own.
steps.because: wins and win points are tracked for each entrant (m_TournamentWinPoints)

steps.do: Do not try to break a tie by hand.
steps.because: the game keeps two tiebreakers of its own, drawn from the opponents each entrant faced (m_TournamentOMW)

steps.do: Read the final order from the entrants rather than from whoever you happened to watch.
steps.because: placement and the prize each entrant receives are recorded per entrant (m_TournamentPlacementIndex)

commonMistakes: Running the standings on paper while the game is keeping its own.
Deciding a tie by who you watched the most.
Leaving the prize shelf empty until the tournament is already over.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
